Title: I'M BUYING KIDNEY OF EXECUTED CHINESE CONVICT
Source.Name: Daily Star
main_content: POORLY Michael Marshall will jet to China to buy a kidney taken from an executed convict. The landscape gardener is so fed-up waiting for an NHS transplant that he is willing to pay GBP 7,000 for an organ removed moments after the criminal's death.The operation will take place in a Chinese hospital specialising in organ swaps. Michael, 35, who has hung on three years for a kidney in Britain, says it is his last chance for life. But last night his plan to cash in on Death Row was slammed by human rights campaigners. They blame the illicit market for the growing number of executions in China for petty crime. Michael, though, insisted he had no choice because there aren't enough donors in Britain. He said: "I don't want to come across as heartless but I don't think there are any moral problems because people are not put on Death Row for nothing. "I have no qualms with receiving a kidney from someone who has been executed." Michael, from York, had a failed second transplant in 1998 after an infection cost him his kidney. He needs dialysis every four hours. He has to make a 75-mile round trip to Leeds for treatment and recently had an operation to remove his jawbone - weakened by the side effects of his illness. Michael had almost given up hope until he saw a documentary about foreigners buying organs from executed Chinese prisoners. He said: "I've already been in touch with Chinese authorities." But Amnesty International said such cases could lead to the death penalty being handed out for even more crimes in China, where 1,077 prisoners were killed last year.
evidence: The article states Michael will buy a kidney from an executed convict in China and has been in touch with Chinese authorities.

Title: I'm so desperate for a transplant I'm going to China to buy a dead convict's kidney
Source.Name: The Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday (London)
main_content: FOR three years Michael Marshall has waited for an NHS kidney transplant while his condition got worse and worse. Now he is so desperate for the chance to reclaim a normal life that he is planning to travel to China to buy the kidney of an executed convict. Mr Marshall contacted the Chinese authorities after seeing a television documentary which told how organs were being removed from prisoners just after they are put to death, and then made available to foreigners.Capital punishment, usually administered by a bullet in the back of the neck, is still common practice in China, and is even carried out for some minor offences. However, Mr Marshall says he has no qualms about the source of the organ he so urgently needs. Nor is he put off by the GBP 7,000 he has to pay for the procedure. 'I have been on dialysis treatment every four hours for the last three years,' he said. 'It is a nightmare and if I have to go to China and get a kidney from an executed criminal then so be it. 'You're not on death row for nothing, ' he added. 'There's risks with any organ you get. If it's going to give me a normal life I'm prepared to take the risk. 'I saw a bit of the television programme and I had to dash to get a note of the telephone number at the end. I rang the number in China and left a message and hope to be contacted soon.' The former landscape gardener from York has already endured two failed transplants, the last in 1998, and now has to make regular trips to Leeds for dialysis treatment. He had to have surgery on his jaw after his condition caused the bone to deteriorate and has just spent three days in York District Hospital to remove fluid from his body. He added: 'I'm serious about this because I can't wait any longer with the NHS. 'I can't see there is any difference in getting a kidney in this way. A healthy kidney is a healthy kidney and I don't think there are any moral problems with what I'm trying to do.' He is on the health service's national list for a new organ. A spokesman for the British Organ Donor Association said of Mr Marshall's plan: 'This practice has been heard of in the past but it isn't something we would recommend or condone.' In recent years there have been a number of investigations concerning the sale of organs from executed prisoners in China to Westerners. In 1998 the FBI arrested two Chinese nationals in New York and accused them of offering to sell organs from prisoners to agents posing as buyers. According to doctors who have defected from the People's Republic, 90 per cent of kidney transplants performed in China involve the use of prisoners' organs. In 1995 U.S. Senators heard that convicts in China were being shot to order to provide corneas and kidneys for Americans at a cost of around GBP 12,000 per organ. Once a deal was made, doctors were ordered to stand by for the operation and a suitable prisoner was promptly executed.
evidence: The article mentions FBI arrests in New York accusing Chinese nationals of offering to sell organs from prisoners to Western buyers. It also states that 90% of kidney transplants performed in China involve the use of prisoners' organs and U.S. Senators heard that convicts in China were being shot to order for Americans.

Title: DAILY STAR SAYS; ORGAN DONOR
Source.Name: Daily Star
main_content: Everyone will have some sympathy for the dying man who wants to travel to China and buy the kidney he desperately needs for GBP 7,000.But the donor will have been executed by a bullet in the back of the head amid fears executions are increasing to feed the transplant trade. There are 100 relatively minor crimes that now merit death in China including fraud, drug peddling and sex offences. How many of us could live knowing an organ donor had suffered that cruel fate? Not a lot.

Title: Brit wants to buy executed man's kidney
Source.Name: Hobart Mercury/Sunday Tasmanian (Australia)
main_content: AN Englishman who has waited three years for a kidney transplant plans to travel to China and buy the organ of an executed criminal. Michael Marshall, 35, of York, contacted Chinese authorities after seeing a television documentary on the trade in organs taken from convicts immediately after execution.AAPThe landscape gardener has already undergone two failed transplants and needs dialysis several times a day. He said he was willing to pay more than $A19,000 for a kidney. "I don't want to come across as heartless but I don't think there are any moral problems because people are not put on death row for nothing," Marshall said. "I have no qualms with receiving a kidney from someone who has been executed. "A healthy kidney is a healthy kidney, whichever body it has been taken from." Capital punishment is still common in China, even for minor offences. It is usually administered by a bullet to the back of the neck.Amnesty International said Marshall's actions could lead to more executions. "China leads the world in executions, killing more than 1000 people a year," an Amnesty spokesman said. "Prisoners are executed usually after grossly unfair trials for crimes as trivial as petty theft and tax evasion, and often within hours of being found guilty. "Organ harvesting could encourage people being killed to order."
